subject: Partner account handoff & tiebreaker guidelines for overlapping territories
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Subject: Partner account handoff & tiebreaker guidelines for overlapping territories

Hi Anna + BlueWave team —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. We have a handful of accounts that show up in both of our pipelines and in some cases also flagged by Nimbus Tools (see BlueWave shared list). I want to propose a short, pragmatic set of handoff/tiebreaker rules so we can avoid mid-quarter surprises and speed up co-sell execution.

Attached: territory_matrix_v3.xlsx — an initial mapping of accounts flagged by either party.

Proposed high-level rules (quick sketch):
- Primary ownership stays with the partner that has an active mutual action plan (MAP) dated within the last 90 days.
- If both partners have a MAP, priority goes to the partner with an existing technical PoC scheduled within 30 days.
- If no MAPs exist, Redwood will default ownership to the partner who has an active reseller agreement + enablement checklist completed.
- For edge cases we escalate to our Partner Ops triage weekly cadence (Fridays).

Request: please review the matrix and reply with any objections or known inaccuracies by EOD Wednesday PST. If you prefer different tie-breakers, flag them in the sheet and we’ll iterate.

Goal: reduce conflicts, avoid duplicate outreach by field reps, and ensure a single point of contact for each account.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Partnerships (North America)
Redwood Inference

Ben / Camila — thanks for the matrix and the clear framework. BlueWave's POV: we support the MAP-first rule but ask that when an account is enterprise (> $250k ARR) we default to a co-sell model with shared ownership unless one party has an executed PoC or closed order. That helps protect existing relationships where both vendors are engaged.

Specifics:
- For H-213 we have an active MAP (signed 2026-07-12) and a technical deep-dive next week — we believe ownership should remain with BlueWave.
- For B-99 we signed a reseller addendum last quarter but PoC is not scheduled yet; we propose priority to the reseller agreement holder (BlueWave).

We don’t object to the escalation cadence, but request that partner contacts be notified 48 hours before any reassignment.

— Anna Matella

Anna — thanks for the color. I put together a concise tiebreaker doc (attached) that folds in BlueWave's enterprise co-sell ask while keeping the operation rules lightweight. Main updates:

1) Enterprise co-sell carve: if ARR > $250k AND both partners are engaged, mark account as "co-sell" and create a shared MAP with designated primary contact for contracting.
2) Notification window: 48-hour notice before ownership flips; ops will send automated Slack + email to the partner POC.
3) Immediate exceptions: any account with an executed PO or signed SOW remains with the closing party.
4) Escalation path: Partner Ops -> Head of Partnerships -> Legal (only for contract conflicts).

Next steps: if there are no major objections, we will publish the guidelines and update the CRM tags on Wednesday 10/07. I've attached partner_handoff_tiebreaker_guidelines.pdf for sign-off.

Sergio Alvarez
